name: Elijah
description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: Elijah delivered the living child to his mother, and she said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year: Go show thyself unto Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth. There was a sore famine in Samaria.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: As Obadiah went his way, Elijah met him; Obadiah fell on his face and said, Art thou my lord Elijah? Elijah told him to go tell Ahab that Elijah is here.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: When Ahab saw Elijah he said, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the trouble on the ordained prophet of God rather than on his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul, so Ahab had thoughts without understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Ahab gathered the prophets and all Israel to Mount Carmel, and Elijah said unto the people, How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him, but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is talking, or pursuing, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be awaked. They cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets till the blood gushed out, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord with twelve stones according to the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob, made a trench about it, laid the wood and the bullock in order, and had them drench the sacrifice with four barrels of water three times until the water filled the trench.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah prayed, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel and that I am thy servant. As the law appointed a sacrifice in the morning and in the evening, this was the evening sacrifice as the sun went down.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: When all the people saw it they fell on their faces and cried, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God. Elijah commanded, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them escape, and they were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there. In the last days it will be the same: when the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for they that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Elijah told Ahab to get up and eat and drink, for there was a sound of abundance of rain. Ahab went up to eat while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees to pray.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: The heaven grew black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain; Ahab rode to Jezreel, a city in the north in Samaria, and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah so that he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had slain all the prophets with the sword. This shows the devil on Ahab: he ran back running his mouth about the slain false prophets and never once mentioned that Elijah had brought rain after a three-year drought.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: Jezebel sent a messenger swearing that she would make Elijah's life as the life of one of the slain prophets by the next day. She wanted him dead because he had taken away her power and the name she had gotten in Israel through her idolatry. This is the same wicked spirit named in Revelation, the top-notch wicked woman who feared no God at all.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: When Elijah heard it he wrapped his face in his mantle and stood in the cave entrance, and the voice asked again, What doest thou here, Elijah? He answered the same, that he was zealous for the Lord and that he alone was left and they sought his life.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and cast his mantle, like a cloak, upon him. Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah, asking to kiss his father and mother first, then he would follow.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: Elisha returned, took a yoke of oxen and slew them, boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave to the people, and they did eat; then he arose and followed Elijah and ministered unto him. He fed the people before he left and then he was gone on his mission, not turning back.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite to go down and meet Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: Elijah takes his mantle, wraps it together, and smites the waters, which divide so the two go over on dry ground. Elijah asks what he shall do for Elisha before he is taken, and Elisha asks for a double portion of his spirit; Elijah says it is a hard thing, granted only if Elisha sees him taken. A chariot of fire and horses of fire part them, and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elisha returns and smites the waters of Jordan with the mantle, asking, where is the Lord God of Elijah, and the waters part so he goes over. The sons of the prophets at Jericho see it and say the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha, and they bow themselves to the ground before him.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Jehoshaphat asks whether there is not a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of the Lord by him. One of the king of Israel's servants answers that Elisha the son of Shaphat is there, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

note.label: 2 Kings 9: Jehu Anointed and the Wicked Kings Cut Off

points: At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: There came a writing to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet, telling him he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat his father nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but in the way of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers. We are the fathers: we reading about ourselves when we read this Bible. We are the Israelites from back then, the good, the bad, and the ugly.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

points: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant. The Lord said he would send Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord; that day has not come yet, so Elijah was sent already.

note.label: The Religious Peer Pressure of Fred Price Jr

points: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the Lord: the sign that we are near the end is that the prophet brought this truth back, the valley of dry bones of Ezekiel 37 and the dead bodies in the street of the great city in Revelation 11 that stood up after three days and a half, and great fear fell on our enemies, which is what you see in these racist towns although we deal civilly with everyone. He shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers: the heart of the fathers is this Bible, the book of our fathers, turned to us the repentant ones, and our minds turned back to it. When we set rules, policies, and orders we go by the word of our fathers, and what is bound on earth is bound in heaven.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

points: And if ye will receive it, this is Elias: John was Elijah.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: Moses and Elias appeared talking with him, so the disciples saw Christ speaking with John the Baptist.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Matthew names him as John the Baptist.

note.label: Mark 9: The Transfiguration, the Dumb Spirit, and Who Shall Be Greatest

points: John confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, nor Elias, nor that prophet.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

cases.name: Elijah
cases.charge: As the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand: shutting the heaven by prayer, standing alone against eight hundred and fifty at Carmel, and running before the king in the hand of the Lord
cases.preview: Elijah the Tishbite of Gilead stood before Ahab and declared, by the Lord God of Israel before whom he stood, that there would be no dew nor rain but by his word (1 Kings 17:1).
